```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

tidydiversity brings biodiversity estimation into the tidyverse. Every
function takes a long data frame, with one row per site and species, and
returns a tibble you can filter, join and plot with the tools you already
use.

```{r setup}
library(tidydiversity)
library(dplyr)
```

## The example data

`ant_gradient` is a **simulated** dataset: counts of 40 ant morphospecies
at eight elevations on two transects. It is synthetic, made for examples,
and is not field data.

```{r}
ant_gradient
```

## Tidy the community

`as_community()` sums repeated records, drops zeros and gives standard
column names. Use your own column names through the `site`, `species` and
`abundance` arguments.

```{r}
ants <- as_community(ant_gradient, .by = transect)
ants
```

If your data arrive as a site by species matrix, `community_long()` turns
it into long format, and `community_wide()` goes the other way.

```{r}
wide <- community_wide(ants, .by = transect)
wide[, 1:6]
```

## Grouping

All verbs accept `.by`, and they respect `group_by()`:

```{r}
ant_gradient |>
  group_by(transect) |>
  div_hill(q = 0) |>
  arrange(desc(diversity))
```
